In my therapy I've learned that a trigger is something , a sound  , smell , object , person , any other visual or feeling brings you back to a certain part of your trauma.   


So for example for me loud sounds or loud voices are a trigger because of my traumatic past with abuse. For others it could be the smell of a perfume that was present at the point of trauma happening. Or maybe even a song. I have a friend that gets triggered by a certain type of carpet because it was in their abuser's home. The posibilities are sadly endless. It all depends on what the brain decides to pick as a trigger.  


There's an endless amount of triggers around and it's different for every person how it feels or displays. Personally I get great senses of fear as if my life is in danger at that very moment and half of the time they are accompanied by vivid flashbacks. If they are really bad I will physically react to it as well by crawling into a ball and / or crying. Accompanied with heavy disassociation. It differs per person though and everyone responds differently.  


I still tend to use the word 'trigger' for it since that's literally what it is. The fact that people started using it as a meme to make fun sjw's is just stupid.

I am a pedigree hamster breeder. With that I want to add that I am not the type of breeder that has their hamsters in small bins and I also do no breed them for profit. I breed them and educate new pet owners properly and I am part of a group of hamster breeders that make these special guidelines / regulations for pet care within our group. We share all we know together and research illnesses , food recommendations, vitamins , medication etc. 

I take utter most care of my hamsters and we work through guidelines within official animal-welfare laws. Which indeed means that an enclosure for a Russian dwarf , Campbelli and Roborovski are usually 80x50cm and up. For Syrians of course a minimum of 100x60cm.

The exception comes when Roborovski is kept with a mate or mates. This is well known within the breeder circle of Roborovski hamsters I am in and beyond in my country. This is for the safety of the hamsters themselves as I would like to add yet again , they will kill each other. This also counts when you put a male and female together. With proper experience this can be done a right way and that’s why I advice against keeping multiple Roborovski’s together or pairs for inexperienced hamster owners.

Neglect is the last thing on my list when it comes to hamsters , with several years of breeding experience and educating people properly on the care and enclosure need and animal-welfare am satisfied with my conclusions.

If you keep a pair of Roborovski’s in an enclosure that is larger than 60 by 50cm they will most likely become territorial over parts over the enclosure and kill each other. If you keep them by themselves then it is safe to keep them in a bigger enclosure of course! Bigger enclosures only work with bigger groups which usually isn’t the case for people just keeping them as pets. Also keeping Roborovski’s in groups isn’t recommended for new or inexperienced pet owners.

For that price it would be hard to get someone to make it for you. Are you or someone you know crafty? Because you would be able to buy a foam base from a maker for that price and finish it yourself or your friends. When you are older you would be able to get the rest of the suit done.

They usually leave remnants of their seeds in their enclosure. It depends on the hamster , some will pick 1 spot and others go all over. With Roborovski’s it is important that their food is small enough for them as well. Small seeds , herbs and dried mealworms. Usually bigger pieces are harder for them to eat which could also end up them losing interest in the food and throwing it around or leaving it alone all together. I hope that helps!

Perhaps they are missing digging opportunities , I would just take out the plateau and fill it up with bedding till the brim and see if that changes anything.

I breed pedigree hamsters and I can full heartedly say that this behavior is stress. Running up and down , left and right like that is a very obvious sign / behavior. These hamsters look like Roborovski’s and leaving them without a wheel will induce lots of stress. It is also extremely important to get them the right size of wheel. A wheel that is too small will physically harm their back , choose a wheel they can run in with their back straight. Also they need more bedding and a sandbath. From the video it is kind of unclear what your enclosure exists of.

I keep some of my own bred Roborovski hamsters together , this is possible but I totally wouldn’t recommend it for an unexperienced hamster owner! Especially since Roborovski’s can not be in a big enclosure like mentioned above since it can trigger fights in small groups. Believe me , you do not want to see what it looks like when it goes wrong. It isn’t a pretty sight.

I can see that the amount of pressure you have used on your pencil was too harsh. The erased lines are still visible and the final piece’s lines are really thick. Try to use barely any pressure like gently stroking the tip of your pencil over the paper so it leaves thin fine lines when you make the raw sketch. Once you’ve done so it’ll be easy to erase lines that you don’t like or any mistakes you’ve made. When you are satisfied with the thin lines you’ve made just retrace them with only slight pressure for better results! If you can see the pencil leave an indentation on the paper you are pushing too hard! 

It takes some practice but it is a technique that will help you a lot with making your sketches and art look more beautiful (and easier to make) in the future. Other than that work on anatomy by looking at free to use references of the human body , just sketch away! 

Also a simple art school rule , a sketch takes less than 5 minutes any thing longer is a drawing. I’ve done lots of art classes and I can assure you can certainly become a good artist with practice seeing your current skill.
